key_insight: This study concerns fetal monitoring, not cancer drug discovery: its Marked DeepHit model predicts the joint probability of imminent delivery and fetal acidosis during labor.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support earlier recognition of deliveries associated with fetal acidosis without assuming that delivery timing is already known.
method: Reframe continuous fetal heart rate and contraction monitoring as time-to-event prediction.
Adapt deep discrete-time survival models and marked point processes to partially observed acidosis labels.
Evaluate predictions at multiple elapsed-time landmarks during labor.
evidence_signal: Marked DeepHit predicted acidemic delivery within one hour with test AUROC 0.837 (95% CI 0.692–0.970) at 6 hours and 0.935 (0.858–0.964) at 12 hours; the abstract also reports validation at a second site.
watch_item: These proof-of-principle results require prospective evaluation before clinical implementation and do not establish improved patient outcomes.
paper_title: Deep Time-to-Event Models for Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring
